title: Multi-tier quant routing with runtime accuracy guardrails
creator: Anika Shah
description: Design and implement a multi-tier runtime kernel selection system that routes requests across FP16 / FP8 / INT8 execution paths using per-model and per-layer quantization profiles. Provide calibration-driven guardrails and online accuracy validation signals to prevent silent quality regressions when lower-precision kernels are chosen. The work spans runtime dispatch logic, calibration integration, offline and online validation suites, and a controlled rollout strategy with automatic fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Routing module implemented that selects kernel path (FP16/FP8/INT8) per-request using model profile + request-level constraints
Integration with calibration store: runtime can query per-model/per-layer scale and clipping parameters and fall back to safe defaults
Offline validation harness produces accuracy delta report per quant profile against baseline FP16 using representative eval sets
Online sampling pipeline emits accuracy signals and KPIs (token-level perplexity drift, response-level semantic similarity) to dashboard
Automatic confidence-gated fallback: if online accuracy drift or latency SLO breach observed, route traffic away from lower-precision path within configured thresholds
End-to-end canary rollout plan with 1%, 5%, 25% phases and automatic rollback on defined thresholds
Unit and integration tests for kernel chooser, calibration fetcher, and fallback circuit respected in CI
Performance regression under 5% median latency increase for typical L/R requests when enabling mixed-precision routing versus baseline FP16 path
updates: 2025-02-04: Initial design review with Applied ML and Runtime teams. Agreed to centralize calibration metadata in the existing calibration-store service and expose a runtime cache with TTL and versioning.

2025-02-07: Decided on a two-layer decision pipeline: 1) static profile selection based on model and routing policy, 2) per-request confidence gate that can override selection using KV cache hit information and request latency budget.

2025-02-10: Prototype of quant-profile fetcher completed. Found that some legacy models lack per-layer scales; added plan to generate synthetic per-layer profiles via offline calibration job and mark as provisional.
2025-02-12: Telemetry schema agreed: we'll emit quant_path, profile_version, per_layer_scale_hash, sampled_ground_truth_id, drift_score, and fallback_reason. Instrumentation spike started.

2025-02-15: Integration test uncovered 8% FP8 accuracy regression on a long-context summarization workload. Follow-up: tighten FP8 per-layer clipping on attention matrices and add a conservative token-level confidence threshold for this workload class.
2025-02-18: Canary orchestration added to console: canary policy config allows decay windows, success thresholds, and mandatory manual approve-to-progress for high customer_impact models.
2025-02-20: Ongoing work: wire up online evaluation sampler, finalize rollback triggers, and prepare runtime-1.21 feature flag for gradual rollout. Assigned PR drafting to ENG-ops for CI gating.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive INT8/FP8 routing yields >2.5x cost reduction on token compute for classification-heavy workloads but increases risk for generative long-context outputs.
Decision rationale: prefer profile-driven static routing to reduce per-request compute on hot paths, but keep confidence gating to catch distributional shifts.
Observability: plan to add a dashboard tile showing 'quantization regret' computed as rolling average difference in semantic-similarity between sampled FP16 and quant-path outputs.

Edge cases: for models using custom ops or fused kernels not yet supported in INT8/FP8, the chooser must mark the layer as "unquantizable" and fall back to FP16 for that layer only (hybrid execution).
